node_definition.done_when: A new tests/test_queue_dag_waits.py covers every arm of section 8's done-when: a request in project A waiting on B:plan#s2 launches only after B's section 2 is declared done, and goes straight to queued when it already is; a cycle through mutual section refs across two plans is refused naming both refs with nothing stored, and so is the mixed cycle where request Y for A#s1 is dispatched --after request X that waits on A#s1; a wait naming a missing section, plan or request is refused at queue time; blocked or failed upstreams move their waiters to blocked-upstream; a complete upstream that is promoted but unmerged keeps its waiter awaiting-upstream and releases it once its promoted_revision is an ancestor of HEAD in the registered checkout, and a row with no promoted_revision holds and raises one obligation; a refused manifest status holds and raises one obligation; gate-held upstream sections in both shapes keep the waiter awaiting-upstream. The readiness re-read calls the roadmap's per-section verdict (project_section_readiness) instead of _readiness_rows' own assembly; RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES narrows to complete; an --after option naming a request id is accepted on any dispatch and carried on TaskNode. The test files importing each changed module add no failures against the base revision, measured serially as a delta with the base and head logs under the run directory; ruff check and ruff format --check pass on the changed paths.
node_definition.goal: Make a queued request's waits follow the work's dependency graph across plans and projects, answered by the roadmap's per-section verdict
